title: Associate Solution Architect
description:
Job Title Associate Architect Role Purpose The Associate Architect is the junior-most architect role, responsible for providing technical ownership and architectural guidance for defined modules, components, or technical workstreams within a project. The role is expected to work closely with Technical/Solution Architects and engineering teams to translate architectural direction into implementable technical solutions, identify technical risks, ensure engineering quality, and contribute to successful technical delivery. The Associate Architect is expected to progressively develop from a technology-focused contributor into an independent technical owner. Key Responsibilities Solution & Architecture Understand functional and non-functional requirements for assigned modules/workstreams. Translate requirements into appropriate technical solutions within the defined architecture. Design components, services, APIs, integrations, data flows, and technical interfaces. Contribute to solution and architecture discussions. Ensure implementation follows defined architecture, standards, and design principles. Identify architectural gaps, dependencies, constraints, and technical risks within the assigned scope. Evaluate technology options and provide recommendations to senior architects. Technical Delivery Take technical ownership of assigned modules/workstreams from design through implementation. Support technical planning, estimation, sequencing, and dependency identification. Work closely with developers and QA engineers during implementation. Provide technical guidance and resolve technical issues within the assigned scope. Ensure technical decisions are documented and communicated to the relevant team members. Support technical readiness and release activities. Technical Quality Ensure code and implementation align with architectural and engineering standards. Promote clean code, maintainability, scalability, security, and performance. Support technical reviews, code reviews, and quality assessments. Identify technical debt and recommend appropriate remediation. Technical Risk Proactively identify technical risks and dependencies. Assess potential impact of technical risks on delivery. Propose mitigation approaches and escalate significant risks to the Technical/Solution Architect. Participate in root-cause analysis and resolution of technical issues. Technology & Engineering Maintain strong hands-on understanding of relevant technologies. Guide developers on appropriate technical implementation approaches. Evaluate new technologies and frameworks relevant to the project. Encourage automation and engineering best practices. AI Adoption & Governance Use approved AI tools to improve development, documentation, testing, analysis, and engineering productivity. Understand responsible AI practices and project-specific AI governance requirements. Ensure AI-generated code or technical outputs are reviewed and validated before adoption. Identify opportunities where AI can improve the assigned technical workstream. Presales Solutioning Support senior architects in technical solutioning activities. Contribute technical inputs to proposals, estimations, solution options, and feasibility assessments. Participate in technical discussions when required. Technical Competencies Strong programming fundamentals and hands-on development experience. Good understanding of software architecture and design principles. Knowledge of object-oriented design, design patterns, APIs, integration, databases, and distributed systems. Understanding of cloud platforms and modern application architecture. Understanding security, performance, scalability, and maintainability considerations. Familiarity with CI/CD and DevOps practices. Familiarity with automated testing and quality engineering practices. Awareness of AI-assisted software development and modern AI engineering tools. Good understanding of Agile software development practices. Behavioral Competencies Strong problem-solving ability. Analytical and structured thinking. Willingness to take ownership. Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly. Collaboration with developers, QA, DevOps, and senior architects. Curiosity and continuous learning mindset. Ability to challenge assumptions constructively. Ability to work independently within defined boundaries. Experience & Qualification Bachelors degree in computer science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related discipline. Typically, 5–8 years of relevant software engineering experience , with demonstrated exposure to architecture/design responsibilities. Strong hands-on technical background. Experience working on enterprise or complex software applications is preferred. 
 Interested candidates please share your updated resume on neelam.fernandes@straive.com. 
 Thanks & Regards, 
 Neelam Fernandes HR Team - Mumbai

Key Skills: Azure Cloud,Microsoft Azure,React.Js,Microservices,AWS,Cloud,Architecture,Microsoft

title: Solution Architect
description:
Your Responsibility: -   1. Solution & Technical Architecture   Own end-to-end solution architecture from business problem to production implementation. Translate business/product requirements into scalable technical solutions. Design application, integration, data, cloud and deployment architectures. Make pragmatic architecture decisions considering scalability, security, cost, performance and speed-to-market. Define APIs, intedaces, integration patterns and service boundaries. Evaluate build-vs-buy decisions and recommend appropriate technologies. Create architecture diagrams, technical specifications and Architecture Decision Records (ADRs). Identify technical risks early and develop practical mitigation approaches.   2. Hands-on Engineering   Remain sufficiently hands-on to prototype, code and troubleshoot solutions when required. Build proof-of-concepts for new technologies and product ideas. Review code and guide developers on engineering practices. Support teams in resolving complex technical and production issues. Establish coding standards, reusable components and engineering guardrails. Work closely with developers rather than operating as an architecture layer outside the engineering team.   The successful candidate should have a “design it, prove it, and help build it” mindset .   3. Data Architecture & Data Modelling   Create conceptual, logical and physical data models. Define database structures, entities, relationships and data flows. Work with relational, NoSQL, time-series and/or event-driven data architectures as appropriate. Design solutions for ingestion, storage, processing and consumption of data. Consider data quality, governance, security, retention and scalability while designing solutions. Understand data architectures required for IoT, analytics and AI-enabled applications.   4. Mobile & Digital Application Architecture   Understand architecture patterns for modern mobile applications across iOS/Android and cross-platform environments. Design backend-for-frontend, API and authentication/authorization architectures supporting mobile applications. Understand push notifications, omine capabilities, device security, synchronization and mobile performance considerations. Design integration between mobile applications, cloud platforms, enterprise systems and connected devices.   5. IoT Architecture   Contribute to solutions involving connected devices, sensors, gateways and industrial IoT. Understand the flow from device/sensor gateway/edge connectivity cloud/IoT platform data application/analytics . 
 Understand common IoT communication and messaging approaches such as MQTT, HTTP/REST and event streaming. Design secure device-to-cloud integration and device/data management approaches. Experience with industrial, manufacturing, energy, logistics, sustainability or asset-monitoring use cases would be advantageous.   6. AI & Agentic SDLC   Understand how AI and autonomous/agentic capabilities can be incorporated into modern software architecture. Have practical exposure to AI-assisted and Agentic Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) approaches. Use AI coding assistants and software engineering agents appropriately across requirements, architecture, coding, testing, documentation and operations. Understand LLM/agent architecture concepts including APIs, orchestration, tool calling, context management, RAG and observability. Help establish appropriate governance and human oversight for AI-generated software. Identify opportunities where agentic workflows can improve developer productivity and accelerate product delivery.   7. Startup / Zero-to-One Product Development   The candidate should have meaningful experience working in environments where the technology organization was still being built.   Expected experience includes: Taking products from idea prototype MVP production scale . Working with incomplete or rapidly evolving requirements. Making technology choices without excessive dependency on established enterprise standards. Balancing technical debt against speed-to-market. Operating with small multidisciplinary teams. Working directly with founders, product leaders, customers and business stakeholders. Taking ownership beyond formal job boundaries when necessary. Building technology foundations that can mature as the business grows. 
 What We Are Looking For: -   Core capabilities   Solution Architecture Technical Architecture Software Engineering / Coding Data Modelling & Database Design API & Integration Architecture Cloud-native architecture Mobile Application Architecture IoT / Connected Device Architecture AI-enabled architecture Agentic SDLC DevOps / CI/CD understanding Security-by-design Architecture documentation and technical decision-making Startup / scale-up product development   Technology Exposure   We are technology-agnostic and value architectural thinking over knowledge of a particular stack. However, strong exposure to several of the following would be beneficial:   Application: Java/Spring Boot, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Node.js, .NET or equivalent modern stacks.   Mobile: Native iOS/Android, Fluer, React Native or similar frameworks.   Data: SQL, PostgreSQL/MySQL, NoSQL, data modelling, event/data pipelines and time-series databases.   Cloud: Azure, AWS and/or GCP; containers, Kubernetes and serverless architectures.   Integration: REST APIs, GraphQL, event-driven architecture, message brokers and microservices.   IoT: MQTT, IoT gateways, edge computing, device management, telemetry and cloud IoT platforms.   AI/Agentic: LLM APIs, AI coding tools, agent frameworks, RAG, vector databases, observability and AI-assisted development workflows.

Key Skills: iot architecture,API,Data Modeling,Agentic Ai,Cloud Architecture,Solution Architect,Cloud,Architecture

title: Solution Architect Core (integration speciality) - Mumbai
description:
Job Description
 Integration Architect & Specialist
 Role Purpose
 The Integration Architect & Specialist will be responsible for designing, governing and enabling enterprise integration architectures that seamlessly connect applications, platforms, data, APIs and external ecosystems.
 The role will define and implement scalable, secure, resilient and reusable integration patterns across legacy and modern technology environments, enabling real-time and batch integration, API-led connectivity, event-driven architecture and seamless business-process orchestration.
 The role will work closely with Enterprise Architecture, Application, Data, Cloud, Cybersecurity, Product and Engineering teams to ensure consistent and robust integration across the enterprise.
 Key Responsibilities
 1. Enterprise Integration Architecture
 * Design end-to-end integration architectures across enterprise applications, platforms, data and external systems.
 * Define integration strategies and architecture patterns across legacy, on-premise, cloud and SaaS environments.
 * Design synchronous and asynchronous integration solutions.
 * Define reusable integration patterns, standards and reference architectures.
 * Ensure integration architectures are scalable, resilient, secure and cost-effective.
 * Identify opportunities to simplify fragmented integration landscapes and reduce point-to-point integrations.
 2. API Architecture & Management
 * Design and govern API-led integration architectures.
 * Define API standards, design principles, lifecycle management and governance.
 * Design RESTful and, where appropriate, GraphQL APIs.
 * Define API security, authentication, authorisation, throttling and versioning.
 * Establish API reuse and discoverability across the enterprise.
 * Support API productisation and external ecosystem integrations.
 * Define API gateway and management architecture.
 3. Event-Driven Architecture
 * Design event-driven and real-time integration architectures.
 * Define enterprise event models and event-driven integration patterns.
 * Design solutions using event streaming and messaging platforms such as Kafka or equivalent technologies.
 * Establish appropriate patterns for:
 * Event publishing
 * Event consumption
 * Event orchestration
 * Event routing
 * Message transformation
 * Retry and failure handling
 * Design architectures capable of supporting high-volume, low-latency transactions.
 4. Integration Platforms & Middleware
 * Architect and evaluate enterprise integration platforms and middleware.
 * Work with technologies such as:
 * API Management
 * Enterprise Service Bus
 * Integration Platform as a Service (iPaaS)
 * Message brokers
 * Event streaming platforms
 * API gateways
 * Workflow/orchestration platforms
 * Define appropriate technology choices based on business and technical requirements.
 * Drive standardisation and rationalisation of integration technologies.
 5. Application & System Integration
 Design integration across:
 Core Applications Digital Channels CRM ERP Data Platforms AI Platforms Partner Ecosystems
 Responsibilities include:
 * Application-to-application integration
 * System-to-system integration
 * Legacy modernisation
 * SaaS integration
 * Cloud integration
 * Partner/B2B integration
 * External API integration
 * Database and data integration
 * File-based integration where required
 6. Cloud & Hybrid Integration
 * Design integration architectures spanning on-premise, private cloud and public cloud.
 * Define hybrid integration patterns.
 * Support cloud migration and application modernisation programmes.
 * Ensure secure connectivity between enterprise environments and cloud platforms.
 * Design for scalability, availability, disaster recovery and business continuity.
 7. Integration Security
 * Incorporate security into integration architecture by design.
 * Define authentication and authorisation mechanisms such as:
 * OAuth 2.0
 * OpenID Connect
 * Mutual TLS
 * JWT
 * API keys where appropriate
 * Ensure encryption in transit and appropriate protection of sensitive data.
 * Design secure external and partner integrations.
 * Work with Cybersecurity and Risk teams to ensure compliance with enterprise security standards.
 8. Integration Reliability & Resilience
 * Design integrations with appropriate:
 * Retry mechanisms
 * Circuit breakers
 * Timeouts
 * Idempotency
 * Error handling
 * Dead-letter queues
 * Failure recovery
 * Transaction management
 * Ensure integrations meet defined availability, performance and resilience requirements.
 * Establish observability and monitoring for integration services.
 9. Integration Governance
 * Define and maintain enterprise integration standards and principles.
 * Review solution designs and ensure compliance with approved architecture.
 * Maintain integration reference architectures and design patterns.
 * Conduct architecture reviews for major integration initiatives.
 * Identify and manage integration technical debt.
 * Ensure consistency across integration implementations.
 10. DevSecOps & Integration Engineering
 * Enable automated deployment and lifecycle management of integration components.
 * Support CI/CD for APIs, integration services and event streams.
 * Establish appropriate testing strategies, including:
 * API testing
 * Contract testing
 * Integration testing
 * Performance testing
 * Security testing
 * Promote Infrastructure as Code and automated configuration management where appropriate.

 Integration Architecture

 * API-led architecture
 * Event-driven architecture
 * Service-oriented architecture
 * Microservices

 * Hybrid integration

 APIs

 Messaging & Events

 Experience with one or more of:
 * MuleSoft

 * 812+ years of experience in Integration Architecture, Solution Architecture, Middleware, API Architecture or related technology domains.

 The successful candidate should demonstrate:

title: Cloud Solution Architect - Enterprise AI Infrastructure and Fin Ops
description:
We are looking for a Cloud Solution Architect whose primary responsibility is to design, build, manage, and optimize the enterprise cloud infrastructure that runs our AI ecosystem. 
 Job Description: 
 Role: Cloud Solution Architect Enterprise AI Infrastructure & FinOps Experience: 1218 years total, with at least 6 years in cloud architecture and at least 3 years architecting production AI/ML or GenAI platforms Education: B.E./B.Tech in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Security, Electronics & Communication, or related Engineering disciplines. Location: Ahmedabad/Mumbai 
 Role Summary The individual hired as Cloud Solution Architect will be responsible for cloud foundation end to end: landing zones, networking, compute, storage, identity, security, Kubernetes platforms, GPU capacity, infrastructure-as-code, monitoring, resilience, and day-to-day infrastructure operations. 
 The role will ensure that AI and GenAI workloads operate securely, reliably, and at scale while driving cloud governance, operational excellence, and FinOps practices to maintain transparency, control, and optimization of cloud and AI spending. 
 This is a hands-on infrastructure leadership role. Application and AI engineering teams build agents and workflows; you make sure the platform they run on is secure, stable, scalable, compliant, and cost-efficient. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 1. Cloud Infrastructure Architecture Own the enterprise cloud infrastructure architecture on Azure, AWS, and/or GCP , including multi-cloud and hybrid designs. Design and maintain enterprise landing zones : management group and account/subscription structure, policies, guardrails, naming and tagging standards, and environment separation (dev, test, validation, production). Architect network infrastructure : hub-and-spoke or Virtual WAN topologies, VNets/VPCs, subnets, private endpoints, DNS, load balancers, application gateways, WAF, ExpressRoute/Direct Connect, site-to-site VPN, and hybrid connectivity to data centers and manufacturing sites. Design compute platforms across VMs, VM scale sets, containers, Kubernetes (AKS, EKS, GKE) , serverless (Functions, Lambda, Cloud Run), and managed PaaS services. Architect storage and database infrastructure: object storage, file shares, managed disks, backup vaults, and managed databases (SQL, PostgreSQL, Cosmos DB, DynamoDB, Redis). Design for high availability, multi-region resilience, disaster recovery, and business continuity with defined RTO and RPO targets. Maintain architecture documentation, reference designs, and architecture decision records (ADRs). 
 2. Cloud Infrastructure Management and Operations Own the day-to-day health, stability, and performance of cloud infrastructure supporting AI and enterprise workloads. Lead infrastructure provisioning, configuration, patching, upgrades, and lifecycle management for VMs, Kubernetes clusters, networking, and platform services. Manage Kubernetes platform operations : cluster upgrades, node pools (CPU and GPU), ingress, service mesh, autoscaling, namespaces, and multi-tenancy for AI teams. Define and track infrastructure SLOs, SLAs, and capacity plans , and lead major incident response, root cause analysis, and problem management. Implement backup, restore, and DR testing on a regular schedule and maintain runbooks. Establish ITIL-aligned processes for incident, change, problem, and service request management in collaboration with IT operations and managed service providers. Manage cloud vendors and managed service partners, including SLA and performance governance. Drive operational automation to reduce manual effort and human error. 
 3. Infrastructure-as-Code, Automation and Platform Engineering Define and enforce infrastructure-as-code standards using Terraform, Bicep/ARM, Pulumi, or CloudFormation. Build reusable IaC modules, templates, and "golden paths" so teams can self-serve compliant infrastructure quickly. Implement CI/CD and GitOps for infrastructure (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, GitLab, Argo CD, Flux). Apply policy-as-code (Azure Policy, AWS SCPs/Config, OPA/Gatekeeper) to prevent misconfiguration and enforce security and cost guardrails. Automate environment provisioning, scaling, patching, compliance checks, and cleanup. Build an internal developer platform experience for AI, data, and application teams. 
 4. AI Infrastructure Enablement Design and operate the infrastructure foundation for AI workloads, covering agent runtimes, workflow engines, data pipelines, model serving, and vector and search services. Provision and manage GPU and accelerator capacity (NVIDIA A100/H100/L40S, Inferentia/Trainium, TPUs) for inference, fine-tuning, and batch processing, including quota management and capacity reservations. Host and secure LLM access infrastructure : Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI, and self-hosted open-source models (vLLM, TGI, Triton, KServe, Ray). Deploy and operate a centralized AI/LLM gateway for secure model access, routing, rate limiting, caching, logging, and cost attribution. Provide infrastructure for agent frameworks and orchestration tools (e.g., LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, Azure AI Foundry, Bedrock Agents, Temporal, Airflow, Logic Apps, Step Functions), including MCP servers and secure tool connectors. Support data platforms used by pipelines, such as Databricks, Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric, Synapse, Kafka/Event Hub, and vector stores (Azure AI Search, OpenSearch, pgvector, Pinecone, Qdrant). Ensure network isolation, private connectivity, and secure integration between AI services and enterprise systems (SAP, LIMS, MES, QMS, document repositories, and on-premises data). Partner with AI engineering teams on LLMOps/MLOps infrastructure: model registries, experiment tracking, CI/CD for AI assets, and environment promotion. Architect the agent runtime platform : hosting, lifecycle management, state and memory, tool execution, session handling, and scaling. Define standards for agent frameworks and patterns (e.g., LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, AWS Bedrock Agents, Azure AI Foundry Agent Service). Design multi-agent orchestration patterns: supervisor/worker, hierarchical, planner-executor, and agent-to-agent (A2A) collaboration. Design the orchestration layer for AI-enabled business workflows combining agents, deterministic logic, APIs, and human tasks. Standardize on durable orchestration and workflow engines (e.g., Temporal, Azure Durable Functions, Logic Apps, AWS Step Functions, Airflow, Prefect, n8n, Power Automate) based on use case. Define event-driven architectures using Kafka, Event Hub, EventBridge, or Pub/Sub for real-time, asynchronous triggers. 
 5. Cloud FinOps and AI Cost Management Establish and run the cloud FinOps practice based on FinOps Foundation principles (Inform, Optimize, Operate) and the FOCUS billing standard. Implement mandatory tagging and cost allocation so every resource and AI workload maps to an owner, cost center, application, agent, workflow, or pipeline. Deliver showback and chargeback reporting to business units and product teams. Track cloud spend across compute, storage, networking, data egress, PaaS services, GPUs, and LLM token consumption . Define unit economics such as cost per agent interaction, cost per workflow run, cost per pipeline execution, and cost per environment. Drive infrastructure cost optimization through: Rightsizing VMs, clusters, and databases Reserved instances, savings plans, and committed use discounts Spot and preemptible capacity for non-critical and batch workloads Autoscaling, scale-to-zero, and scheduled shutdown of non-production environments Storage tiering, lifecycle policies, and orphaned resource cleanup GPU utilization improvement and workload consolidation LLM cost controls such as model routing, caching, batch APIs, and provisioned throughput decisions Set budgets, quotas, and anomaly alerts per subscription, team, and AI workload. Produce forecasts and executive dashboards linking cloud and AI spend to business value. Support Finance and Procurement on enterprise agreements, commitments, and vendor negotiations. 
 6. Cloud Security and Compliance Design and enforce cloud security architecture based on zero-trust principles . Own identity and access architecture (Entra ID, AWS IAM, GCP IAM), RBAC, privileged access management, managed identities, and workload identity for agents and services. Implement secrets and key management (Key Vault, KMS, HashiCorp Vault), encryption at rest and in transit, and certificate lifecycle management. 
 7. Monitoring, Observability and Reliability Architect enterprise monitoring and observability for infrastructure and AI workloads using Azure Monitor, CloudWatch, Google Cloud Operations, Datadog, Dynatrace, Prometheus/Grafana, and OpenTelemetry. Monitor infrastructure health, performance, capacity, GPU utilization, network latency, and cost in unified dashboards. Integrate AI-level telemetry (token usage, latency, failures) from tools such as Langfuse or LangSmith with infrastructure observability. Apply SRE practices : error budgets, proactive alerting, chaos testing, and post-incident reviews. 
 8. Technical Leadership and Governance Act as the design authority for cloud infrastructure , reviewing and approving infrastructure designs from project and product teams. Define cloud standards, policies, and best practices, and drive consistent adoption across teams. Lead and mentor cloud engineers, DevOps/platform engineers, and operations staff. 
 Required Skills and Experience 12+ years in IT infrastructure, with at least 7 years of hands-on cloud infrastructure architecture and operations on Azure, AWS, or GCP (multi-cloud preferred).
